newsitem.title: FRANCE: Investors to challenge BNP board - paper.
newsitem.headline: Investors to challenge BNP board - paper.

text.p: BNP-Intercontinentale stockholders are expected to challenge Banque Nationale de Paris (BNP) on Wednesday on its handling of the buyout of BNP-Intercontinentale minorities, the Financial Times reported on Wednesday.

The newspaper said the challenge would be led by a group representing more than 10 percent of the shares in the BNP-Intercontinentale (BNP-I) subsidiary at the unit's annual general meeting, which is open only to shareholders.

It said the investors, assisted by French corporate governance crusader Sophie L'Helias, were concerned about the terms of the buyout, the lack of financial information available on BNP-I and a lack of independent directors on its board.
BNP, which holds 70 percent of BNP-I, is offering three BNP shares for each BNP-I share. The terms were announced after the deadline for resolutions for the BNP-I shareholders meeting.
The Financial Times said one institutional investor estimated the net asset value of BNP-I at 1,200 francs per share, compared with BNP's offer of about 750 francs based on Tuesday's closing price.
It quoted BNP as saying the offer had been carefully examined to ensure that it was fair.
BNP-I holds controlling and minority stakes in financial institutions in financial centres and emerging markets, notably in the Middle East.
